title: No eligible citizen is left out (?)
shows: Aman Bhargava of Diagram Chasing tests the line printed on every page of Karnataka's final roll summary, that no eligible citizen is left out and no ineligible person is included, against the rolls themselves. He read all 60,923 booth files of the final roll of 27 October by machine and joined them by EPIC number to digitised copies of the 2002 roll, the January 2025 roll, the list of names left off the draft and the notice lists, which the groups Mathakaavalu and Edellu Karnataka made. He reports that of 1,05,48,148 electors left off the draft whom he found on the January 2025 roll, about 14,900 came back on the final roll in the same constituency with the same name, relative and age, and that 206 of 8.9 lakh aged 75 and over came back. He counts 3,115 electors told they were not on the 2002 roll although the Chief Electoral Officer's own copy of it carries them under the same EPIC number, 4,954 deleted after a notice that flagged children born less than nine months apart, a rule that catches twins, 8,992 people on the roll more than once in their own booth, 461 EPIC numbers on the roll in two constituencies and 234 new voters in Dasarahalli given an EPIC number held earlier by someone left off the draft. He finds the share of electors sent a notice ranging from 0.03 per cent in Mayakonda to 59 per cent in C.V. Raman Nagar, and nine constituencies where no notice ended in a finding of ineligibility. He says his counts are minimums, that matching by name, relative and age cannot establish identity, and that the work rests on optical character recognition of files the Commission publishes only as PDFs.
quote: Since rolls by themselves cannot conclusively establish identity, all duplicate counts or anomalies should be considered minimum figures.
About 14,900 people were added back, which is 0.14%.
note: First reading, 13 November 2026, of the page read in full and rendered in a browser. The byline gives Aman Bhargava and 12 November 2026. The page names individual electors and links the Election Commission's booth PDFs and a row-level dataset, and none of those names or links is carried here. The 14,900 counts only those who came back in the same constituency under the same name, relative and age, so it is a floor, and the summary says how it was counted. The film-titled framing and the author's closing views on cost and on the Commission are not carried.
